## 3. The evidence that moved it





**The pretrained component is removed, and the method still works.**
[39384986](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39384986/) (*Nat Methods*): de novo protein design with a denoising
diffusion network **independent of pretrained structure-prediction models**. The
foundation-model thread's claim is that scale and pretraining produce
transferable general-purpose models. A title announcing independence from
pretraining as the contribution is the cleanest available refutation of that
claim, and it is a constructive one — the ablation is the result.

**A generalist biomedical vision-language model.** [39112796](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39112796/) (*Nat Med*)
runs in the other direction in the same month. November 2024 has both the
generalist claim and its ablation.

**[39546375](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39546375/): an agent pointed at a working scientist's own data.** LmRaC
lets an LLM interrogate user experimental results. The agentic thread's claim is
about research *infrastructure* rather than demonstrations, and a tool that takes
a user's own unpublished results as input is infrastructure by that definition.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

The diffusion-without-pretraining paper above is the refutation and is filed on
`foundation-models`.

### (b) Method credibility

November 2024 is thin here, which is a real contrast worth stating precisely: in
November 2025 this thread takes ten cards, its largest month. Under the
consistent-rule scan run on 2026-08-26, the 2024 monthly counts run between one
and eight with a median of three, and the 2025 counts are statistically
indistinguishable from them. The visible difference between November 2024 and
November 2025 in *this file* is mostly a difference in how hard each month was
read, which is the error the whole corpus has been correcting for.
